system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

USSD messages using the default alphabet are coded with the GSM 7-bit default alphabet given in clause 6.2.1. The message can then consist of up to 182 user characters. Cell Broadcast messages using the default alphabet are coded with the GSM 7-bit default alphabet given in clause 6.2.1. The Message Information Page then consists of 93 user characters. (Federal Emergency Management Agency [FEMA]) Los Angeles County may have avoided damage to people outside the impacted Kenneth Fire area had their message included more information on the location or the timing of the danger. This additional information is also important for people who have older phones, where geotargeting is not precise on those devices. data.summary: English text is 317 GSM-7 characters across 4 pages, which matches the 93 characters per page and is well under the 15-page maximum. No languages are required under the GENERIC profile. However, the first page (first 93 characters) holds only the preamble and issuer. It does not carry the hazard or the action, so a handset that shows only page 1 delivers neither.

objections.issue: Page 1 (the first 93 GSM-7 characters) is taken up by 'NEW: This is an emergency message from the Los Angeles County Fire Department.' and cuts off at about 'An EVACUATION W…'. The hazard (evacuation warning, fire) and the action (be ready to evacuate) fall on page 2.
objections.fix: Put the hazard and action at the start, e.g. 'EVACUATION WARNING (fire) for [named area]: be ready to evacuate now. Gather loved ones, pets, supplies. –LA County Fire Dept. More: alertla.org'. Keep the hazard and action within the first 93 characters, and drop or shorten the 'This is an emergency message from' preamble.

evidence.quote: The Message Information Page then consists of 93 user characters.
NEW: This is an emergency message from the Los Angeles County Fire Department.

no_basis.concern: 'Your area' gives no location, which matters on older handsets with imprecise geotargeting. This is mainly a content issue for the drafter or approvers, not a delivery one.
